intro: Step quietly into Eşrefoğlu Mosque, a mosque and complex in Konya province, built in 1297–1299. Look around you: forty-two cedar columns carry a wooden ceiling that is still in place after seven centuries. At the centre, the snow well is left open, so that winter snow can keep the timber from drying out.
history: The mosque was built between 1297 and 1299 for Eşrefoğlu Süleyman Bey. It is the largest and best preserved of Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques: for seven centuries, forty-two cedar columns have carried its flat timber ceiling. In 2023 it became one of those inscribed as the Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the cedar columns, the snow well, the tiled mihrab, the wooden minbar and, as you come or go, the portal.
facts: Did you know? The snow well at the centre is engineering, not ornament. In winter, snow falling through the roof melts and evaporates, keeping the air damp enough that the timber does not split. None of the forty-two cedar columns has ever been replaced: the same trees have carried the roof for seven centuries. And in 2023 Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques entered the World Heritage List — with Eşrefoğlu the largest of them all.
outro: This brings our visit to Eşrefoğlu Mosque to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. As you step back outside, remember the old cedars still holding up the roof. Enjoy your visit.
